humanOnly.note: Guardian never runs these and never auto-chains into them; it tells the employee exactly what to type. None of these plugins enforces it (no disable-model-invocation), so Guardian enforces it as a text-level rule.

commands.why: QA sign-off of the readiness verdict
duplicate / won't-fix is a human decision

humanOnly.approvalEdits: Flipping a planning document's status (proposed→approved, draft→approved, draft→ready-for-qa) is the employee's decision — never edit it on their behalf, even when they ask you to; tell them the file and line to change.

intents.label: Build a new feature (mobile / TV / React web)
requires: work branch (the plugin blocks every file write on main/master)
intents.gates: Each stage needs the previous document approved by a human (status field).
intents.next: Feature-flow commands (0.8.0+) end with a next_command Continue offer, like the bug flow — follow it after the employee says yes, unless it is in humanOnly.commands or an approval edit.

intents.label: Continue implementing a task
requires: FA, DD, Dev Plan and Task Breakdown approved

intents.label: Fix a bug
intents.next: Bug-flow helpers print a next_command JSON ({skill, args, display}) — follow it after the employee says yes — unless it is in humanOnly.commands (e.g. /verify-fix-cycle): then tell them what to type.

intents.label: Review code
intents.note: Internal review of the employee's OWN changes in this checkout. scope = a branch or path to diff against: review A into B = on A, /review-code B (origin/B if the local B is missing or behind). A pull request URL is never a scope (0.8.0 stops and offers /review-pr): someone else's PR → the review-pr intent.

intents.label: Review a teammate's pull request
examples: a PR from the opener's review list
intents.args: <exact GitHub or Bitbucket Cloud PR URL>
intents.note: Read-only, no checkout, no clean tree needed, works from any repo. Pass the URL exactly as gh / Bitbucket gave it (a PR number alone → get its URL with gh pr view <n> --json url). GitHub uses the employee's gh login; Bitbucket needs BITBUCKET_API_TOKEN in the environment (the command says how). Posting, approving or requesting changes stays the employee's call.
requires: dev plugin 0.8.0+ (commands/review-pr.md under its installPath — scripts/dev-plugin.sh has-review-pr)

intents.label: Pre-PR regression check (what could my change break?)
intents.note: Owned by the dev plugin since 0.8.0 (Guardian's own pre-PR skill is removed — no fallback). It refuses until development, developer testing and a fresh internal review with no Blocking finding are done, and says what comes first. Ends with a PRE_PR {…} line for display; decisions come from the readiness contract (scripts/dev-plugin.sh readiness). No dev plugin in the session → no pre-PR is required and none is run.

intents.label: Hand a finished feature or fix to QA
Prepare a mobile release
intents.gates: The final Go is a human decision.

intents.label: Sync the React Native theme from Figma
QA for mobile / TV apps: test plan, execution, bugs, readiness
requires: launched from the workspace folder that holds the code repo and the QA repo (name contains "qa")
intents.pickWhen: Mobile or TV app under test (iOS, Android, React Native, tvOS, Android TV), Appium automation, a QA workspace with a code repo + QA repo.

intents.label: Understand / onboard to this repo, generate CLAUDE.md and project docs
intents.notes: /inspect always stops at a menu for the employee's choice.

resume.note: Probes for "you're at stage X of feature Y". Documents are the source of truth; tool state files are hints. scripts/resume-state.sh implements these deterministically (formats in docs/resume-state.md) and runs at session start; the probes below are the fallback when it is silent or unsure.

ono-mobile-dev-plugin.feature: Dev plugin 0.8.0+: node --no-warnings "<installPath>/scripts/feature-flow.ts" status --root <repo> --feature <F> → stage, the human approval it waits on (waiting_on[].where = <path>:<line>) and next_command. Older: planning docs by YAML frontmatter (doc_schema_version + feature:) · FA proposed → approval · DD (*-DD.md) missing/draft → design · Task Breakdown missing/draft → tasks · docs/tasks/<F>-task-state.json partial → implementing · docs/reviews/<F>/review.md missing → /review-code --feature <F> · qa_handoff_link set → QA.
ono-mobile-dev-plugin.bug: docs/bugs/<key>/ exists → node --no-warnings "<plugin>/scripts/analyze-bug.ts" start bug:<key> --root <repo> (status + next_command).

ono-plugin-qa.feature: In the QA repo: no <slug>/test-plan.md → not started · status in the fenced ```yaml block at the top (draft|approved) · approved without coverage-report.md → waiting for dev handoff · then node "<plugin>/scripts/qa-ledger.mjs" view execution|bugs|regression|readiness --scope feature:<slug> --qa-repo <path> (read-only JSON). Never call readiness render/signoff.

ono-project-inspector.repo: AUDIT.md topic statuses + CLAUDE.md / docs/project/ existence are the truth; .ono/state.json resume.nextAction is a hint (may be stale). Or route to /inspect-status.

gitGuards.note: Org-plugin hooks that block Claude's own git writes. In these repos Guardian hands the exact git / gh commands to the employee (they can run them with the ! prefix) instead of running them.
gitGuards.matrix-qa-plugin: Any repo with matrix-qa.config.json at or above the session folder: every git write and gh pr create is denied (also blocks other repos in the same session). Reported as guards.matrixQa.
gitGuards.ono-plugin-qa: git commit / push blocked in the QA repo: the repo named by .claude/qa-workspace.json qaRepoPath, else any repo whose folder name contains "qa". Reported as guards.onoQaCommitBlocked.
gitGuards.ono-mobile-dev-plugin: Every Write/Edit is blocked on main/master (docs too); code edits ask for approval; secrets in written content are blocked.
